stories.headline: Gibbs Gets the Biggest Payday Any Ball-Carrier Ever Saw, and the Whole Territory Just Got Richer
stories.read: Detroit backed the wagon up to Jahmyr Gibbs and unloaded sixty-seven and a half million over three years, fifty-one and a half of it guaranteed, which makes him the best-paid runner in the whole territory. Same week Indianapolis handed Jonathan Taylor forty-four million to stay put, so the fellas who tote the rock are eating good in 2026. Here is what matters to your outfit, pardner: every nervous manager who had Gibbs sliding down the board over that camp absence has got no excuse left, and Detroit does not hand a man that much money to split the haul with anybody. The discount closes today. If somebody in your saloon is still spooked, go swap horses with him before sundown.

stories.headline: Arizona's Backfield Is Wide Open and a Rookie Is Standing in the Middle of It
stories.read: James Conner still has not taken a single 11-on-11 rep in camp, Trey Benson got held out of the Hall of Fame Game with a sore knee, and the Cardinals list rookie Jeremiyah Love as RB2 while he keeps running with the first team anyway. Nathaniel Hackett will not say the words out loud, but the pecking order at that ranch is telling on itself. The No. 3 overall pick is 214 pounds of trouble and the saloon is still pricing him like a spare horse. Doc's read: this is the exact shape of a diamond in the rough, a fella one week from a bell-cow workload at a price nobody has corrected yet. Go stake that claim before the herd wakes up.

stories.headline: Ja'Tavion Sanders Is Turning Into a Dry Well in Carolina
stories.read: The preseason opener told on the Panthers something fierce. Sanders started, played the whole first drive, then vanished while lesser men kept taking snaps, and he has already slid to third on the unofficial pecking order behind Mitchell Evans. Time was, folks called him cheap gold at tight end. Now he is a third-down specialist who might not even hold a roster spot. Doc says cross him off and look sideways instead: with rookie Chris Brazzell laid up for the year, Xavier Legette is the clear No. 3 pass-catcher in that camp and John Metchie is one Jalen Coker tweak away from real work. That is where the money is.
